sections.Intro: A heart medicine, after rheumatism or influenza, where the muscles of the heart are in stage of fatty degeneration, regulating the pulse and increasing the power of contractions of heart, with increased urinary secretions. Valvular affections. Most valuable in cardiac dropsy. Low vitality, with weak heart and slow, pulse. Hydrothorax, ascites.
sections.Head: Feels light; aches across front, from occiput around temples to eyes. Vertigo on rising, turning head quickly or lying down. Tinnitus. Scalp feels tight.
sections.Mouth: Slimy. Tongue dirty yellow, sore, feels scalded.
sections.Heart: Mitral and aortic regurgitation. Praecordial pain, palpitation, and dyspnoea. Marked venous engorgement. Cardiac asthma. [Quebracho.] Fatty heart. Myocarditis, irregular cardiac action, constriction and vertigo. Pulse rapid, irregular.
sections.Stomach: Heavy weight. Gnawing hunger. Faint feeling in epigastrium. Better out of doors.
sections.Urine: Oily pellicle on urine. Scanty, albuminous.
sections.Respiratory: Frequent desire to take a long breath. Feeling of weight on chest.
sections.Extremities: Aching in nape. Spine stiff and aching.
sections.Relationship: Adonidin is a cardiac tonic and diuretic. Quarter to half grain daily, or two to five grains of first decimal trit. Increases arterial pressure and prolongs the diastole, favoring emptying engorged veins. Compare; Digit.; Cratseg.; Conval.; Strophantus.
sections.Dose: Five to ten drops of the tincture.
